title: Map of Wallachia
creator: Constantin Cantacuzino, stolnic; printed by Chrysanthos

title: Descriptio Moldaviae - map
creator: Dimitrie Cantemir
note: The manuscript travelled to Russia; the print carried the content.

title: Hereford Mappa Mundi
creator: Circle of Richard of Haldingham (attrib.)
scope: The whole orbis terrarum arranged on a theological schema
note: Reproduction rights for any specific witness image are not cleared by this value.

title: Chorographia Transylvaniae
creator: Johannes Honterus
edition_state: One known impression of the 1532 woodcut
repository: Repository unconfirmed - recorded as likely Budapest

title: Josephinische Landesaufnahme
creator: Habsburg General Staff plane-table parties
scope: The Habsburg lands including Transylvania; Oltenia and Moldavia lie outside it
note: Classified from birth and therefore complete.

title: Notitia Dignitatum omnium tam civilium quam militarium
creator: Unknown late Roman compilers of the imperial chancery
witness: A lost late-antique original known through Carolingian and later copies; the Speyer codex from which they descend is itself lost
repository: Copies in several European collections; the register is read through printed editions
scope: The offices and commands of the late Roman empire, east and west. It enumerates administrative units and the officers who held them; it depicts nothing and locates nothing, so it can attest that a name was in official use without attesting where anything was.
note: Cited structurally rather than by page: the register's own divisions are the locator. Neither the edition nor any copy has been opened for this corpus, which is why the record stays normalized.

title: Dacia - Parergon
creator: Abraham Ortelius
scope: Antiquarian reconstruction of the ancient provinces over modern geometry
note: An antiquarian restoration; readings from it are reconstructed rather than contemporary.

title: Geographia III.8 - Dacia
creator: Klaudios Ptolemaios
witness: Manuscript tradition; editio princeps with maps
scope: A coordinate catalogue of Dacia between the Tisia the Danube and the Hierasus; towns and tribes only
note: Survives as numbers; every drawn map of it is a later restoration.

title: Roman Imperial Coinage: the Dacia reverse types
creator: H. Mattingly, E. A. Sydenham and successors
witness: The coins themselves, catalogued as a series; the reference work is the access to them
repository: Specimens in the major cabinets; the catalogue is widely held
scope: Imperial coin types arranged by reign. It records what a mint struck and what legend it carried, which is a use of a name by the state itself rather than a description of a place.
note: The volume and number for each Dacia type is not transcribed here; the record cites the series and stays normalized until a specimen is checked.

title: Russian General Staff map
creator: Russian General Staff
scope: The Principalities under Russian administration; the survey stops at the mountains
note: First geodetic lattice for the region.

title: Planurile directoare de tragere and their classified successors
creator: Serviciul Geografic al Armatei, with the French military mission of 1916-17
witness: A series, not a sheet: some 2,118 sheets at 1:20,000 on the Lambert-Cholesky grid, continued after 1951 on Gauss-Kruger
repository: Military archives; the series is georeferenced sheet by sheet by geo-spatial.org
citation: Planurile directoare de tragere, 1:20,000 (Serviciul Geografic al Armatei, 1916-1959)
scope: The state territory as an artillery surface, Transylvania included after 1920; the most complete survey of the land and the least publishable
note: One row for the series: a member sheet is cited per attestation through locator_type sheet, which is where a sheet identifier belongs. Reviewing this record means reading the series scope, not one sheet.

title: Charta României Meridionale
creator: Commonly attributed to Carol Popp de Szathmári
scope: The united Principalities; the first deliberately public state map of the country
note: The point at which ROMÂNIA is printed officially in Latin type.

title: Tabula Peutingeriana segm. VII–VIII
creator: Unknown imperial compilers; medieval copyist
edition_state: Medieval copy of a late-antique original
scope: The cursus publicus; road stations and mileages rather than settlement generally
note: Dated by its fourth-century content rather than its c. 1200 parchment, following the trench's stated rule.

title: Portolan chart
creator: Pietro Vesconte
scope: Mediterranean and Black Sea coastlines; the interior is not surveyed
note: Scope is what makes inland silence extra_muros rather than omission.
